hook: A synapse scaffold protein is essential at fly high-release synapses but mostly unneeded at low-release ones
hook_turn: is essential at fly high-release synapses but mostly unneeded at low-release ones
summary: At the fruit fly neuromuscular junction, the protein RIM was required for transmission at a high-release-probability input but largely dispensable at a neighboring low-release input. It was also needed for rapid plasticity only at the high-release input, where super-resolution imaging showed it sits closer to calcium channels. The results come from one fly synapse type, so they may not generalize to mammals.
title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity.
